title: Bounded-projective cone and scalar calculus on w-contractible affines
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and put $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$. For a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], let $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and write $D(T,\Lambda)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_T)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Dualizable means admitting evaluation and coevaluation for derived tensor with unit $\Lambda_T[0]$, satisfying both triangle identities. Put $L_T(P)=\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline P$ for the canonical scalar realization [def-zl-condensed-scalar-realization], where underlines are discrete constant sheaves. A perfect ring complex is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

Let $T$ be w-contractible affine [sk-def-pe-wlocal], put $B=\Gamma(T,\Lambda_T)$, and let $F_T:D(B)\to D(T,\Lambda)$ send $Q$ to $\Lambda_T\otimes^L_{\underline B}\underline Q$ using the constant-section map. The following representative calculus holds.

For any morphism $f:Q\to Q'$ between perfect $B$-complexes, and any bounded finite-projective representatives $q^\bullet,q'^\bullet$, there is a chain map representing $f$. Its cone $c^n=q'^n\oplus q^{n+1}$ is bounded finite-projective. The cone of $F_T(f)$ is isomorphic to $F_T(c^\bullet)$ and is dualizable. The objects $F_T(0)$ and $F_T(Q)[m]$ are dualizable for every perfect $Q$ and every $m\in\mathbf Z$; dualizability is invariant under isomorphism. Every morphism between dualizable objects in $D(T,\Lambda)$ is isomorphic to an $F_T(f)$ as above.

For every perfect $P\in D(R)$, the complex $B\otimes_R^L P$, formed with the derived scalar extension along $R\to B$ [def-zl-ring-derived-scalar-extension], is perfect and there is a natural derived isomorphism $L_T(P)\simeq F_T(B\otimes_R^L P)$; in particular $L_T(P)$ is dualizable. This assertion holds for every commutative condensed $\Lambda$, without flatness of $B$ over $R$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] to this w-contractible affine $T$: its functor is exactly $F_T$, and it is exact and fully faithful and induces $\operatorname{Perf}(B)\simeq D_{\mathrm{lis}}(T,\Lambda)$. In particular every perfect $B$-complex has dualizable image. For a map $u:K\to K\prime$ between dualizable objects choose isomorphisms $a:F_T(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ and $b:F_T(Q\prime)\xrightarrow{\sim}K\prime$ with $Q,Q\prime$ perfect. Fullness supplies $f:Q\to Q\prime$ with $F_T(f)=b^{-1}ua$. Thus $(a,b)$ is an isomorphism from the arrow $F_T(f)$ to $u$.

source.place: Lemma 4.1(1)-(2), applied to the ordinary derived categories as stated by the cited node

proof.text: Fix the specified representatives $q^\bullet,q\prime^\bullet$ and their isomorphisms to $Q,Q\prime$. Transport $f$ along those isomorphisms. The source complex is bounded above with projective terms, so [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-representative] represents the transported morphism by a homotopy class of chain maps; choose a chain map $v$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], its cone has $c^n=q\prime^n\oplus q^{n+1}$ and $d_c^n(y,x)=(d_{q\prime}^ny+v^{n+1}x,-d_q^{n+1}x)$. The chain-map identity gives $d_c^{n+1}d_c^n=0$. Outside the union of the two finite degree intervals its terms vanish. A direct sum of two finitely generated projectives is again such: generators are the two finite generating sets, and lifts along any surjection are constructed separately on each summand using the projective lifting property. Hence $c$ is a bounded finite-projective complex and represents a perfect object.

source.place: Tag 066R, lemma-two-out-of-three-perfect, conclusion; explicit cone proof written by the agent using the cited Mathlib chain-map representative leaf

proof.text: The cone triangle of $v$ is distinguished by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Exactness of $F_T$ from [lem-zl-condensed-wcontractible-lisse-evaluation] sends it to a distinguished triangle with first arrow isomorphic to $F_T(f)$. Its third object $F_T(c)$ is dualizable by the perfect-to-lisse equivalence. To compare with any chosen cone of $F_T(f)$, TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] extends the isomorphism on the first two vertices to a morphism of distinguished triangles. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] its third map is an isomorphism, giving the asserted cone isomorphism. The zero complex and every shifted complex $q[m]$ are bounded finite-projective, so their images are dualizable; exactness identifies $F_T(q[m])$ with $F_T(Q)[m]$. Finally, for an isomorphism $h:K\xrightarrow{\sim}K\prime$ and a dual $D$ of $K$, use evaluation $D\otimes K\prime\xrightarrow{1\otimes h^{-1}}D\otimes K\to\Lambda_T$ and coevaluation $\Lambda_T\to K\otimes D\xrightarrow{h\otimes1}K\prime\otimes D$. The two triangle identities reduce to those of $K$ by cancelling $h^{-1}h$ and $hh^{-1}$. This proves invariance under isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose a bounded finite-projective representative q of P. Bounded complexes of flat objects are K-flat by the existing Mathlib/source API. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-right-adjoint-kflat-representative] to ordinary extension and exact restriction of scalars with the fixed derived adjunction of [def-zl-ring-derived-scalar-extension], constructed by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-scalar-adjunction]. Its localized-unit transpose is invertible on q, so the specified derived scalar extension is isomorphic to termwise extension. The latter has the same bounds and finite-projective terms from Step 4, hence is perfect. The source helper for same-universe functorial flat resolutions is the proved private helper of the scalar-adjunction module, imported with import all; extension preserves K-flat quasi-isomorphisms by lem-pc-extension-kflat-quasi-iso.

The three transparent specializations abbreviate its A, F and D. projectiveCalculusScalarSection computes pullback of a scalar section from the point; the theorem requires the scalar ring homomorphism to have exactly this underlying function. Thus no arbitrary scalar map or flatness assumption is substituted. Natural comparison is stated on the full subcategory of perfect scalar complexes.
